notes.note: Title of the page of the recursive resolver and its entry in the browser tab.
Entry of the DNS sub-navigation that leads to the recursive resolver.
Heading of the trust anchors, the keys that DNSSEC validation starts from.
Empty state of the trust anchors when the server lists none.
Heading of the negative trust anchors, names under which DNSSEC validation is switched off for a while.
Label of the root hints, the addresses of the root servers that the resolver starts from.
Label of the time the resolver last asked the root servers for the list of root servers.
Heading of the infrastructure cache, what the resolver remembers about name servers.
DNSSEC validation state: the answer is proven genuine.
DNSSEC validation state: the zone is provably not signed.
DNSSEC validation state: the signatures are wrong or missing, so the answer is refused.
DNSSEC validation state: validation could not reach a result.
DNSSEC validation state: nothing validated the answer.
How a view resolves names it does not serve: the resolver iterates from the root.
How a view resolves names it does not serve: through the default forwarder.
How a view resolves names it does not serve: it refuses them.
How a view resolves names it does not serve: as the profile says.
Mode of a forwarding rule that resolves the names under its suffix iteratively instead of forwarding them.
Preset in the forwarding rule dialog: one rule for all names to a resolver that is reached over DNS over TLS.

segment.source: Forward everything to a DoT resolver

notes.note: Column of the cache table: the DNSSEC validation state of the entry.
Extended DNS error (RFC 8914) of a bogus entry; {code} is the info code number.
Explains the extended DNS error code shown next to the state of an entry; {code} is the info code number.

segment.source: Extended DNS error {code} (RFC 8914), sent with the failure answer

notes.note: Explains when the signatures of a validated entry expire; {time} is a date and time.
Heading of the block that shows the recursive resolver of this server's DNS node.
Tag that says the recursive resolver of the node is running.
Shown while the state of the recursive resolver is being read.
Shown on the recursion page when this server has no DNS node, so there is no resolver to show.

segment.source: This server has no DNS node, so there is no resolver to show.

notes.note: Heading of the note that says the node's recursive resolver is switched off.
Explains that the resolver is off and where it is switched on; enabled and [dns.recursion] are names in the configuration file and stay as they are.

segment.source: The node answers from its own zones and its forwarders only. Set enabled in the [dns.recursion] section of tenko.toml to resolve names from the root.

notes.note: Heading of the card with the hints and the last priming of the recursive resolver.
Source of the root hints: the list that ships with the product.
Label of the date of the root hints.
Shown when the resolver has not primed itself yet.
Tag: the last priming succeeded, a root server answered.
Tag: the last priming failed, no root server answered.
How long the last priming took; {ms} is a number of milliseconds.
Label of the time the resolver's list of root servers expires and the next priming is due.
Button that asks the node to prime its resolver now.
Confirms that the node was asked to prime its resolver.
Title of the error when the node could not be asked to prime its resolver.

segment.source: The priming could not be requested

notes.note: Heading of the warning that lists what the recursive resolver reports as wrong.
Problem of the resolver: no root server answered the priming query.

segment.source: No root server answered the priming query, so recursed names are answered SERVFAIL until a priming succeeds.

notes.note: Heading of the table of root servers the resolver uses.
Column of the root servers table: the name of the server.
Column of the root servers table: the address in use.
Column of the root servers table: the smoothed round-trip time to the server.
Shown for a root server that has not answered yet, so its round-trip time is unknown.
A time in milliseconds; {ms} is formatted already.
Label of the number of zone cuts the infrastructure cache holds.
Label of the number of name server addresses the infrastructure cache holds.
Label of the number of name server names the infrastructure cache holds.
How full a cache is; {count} is what it holds and {max} its bound, both formatted already.
Heading of the counters of the resolver since the role started.
Counter: client queries the resolver answered with an answer or NXDOMAIN.
Counter: client queries the resolver answered with SERVFAIL.
Counter: client queries stopped because they used up their budget of queries, restarts or depth.
Counter: client queries that ran out of time.
Counter: client queries answered from locally served zones.
Counter: client queries answered SERVFAIL from the failure cache without asking an authority server.
Counter: queries the resolver sent to authority servers.
Counter: answers from authority servers that were dropped as unwanted.
Column of the query log: how the answer was found.
Column of the query log: the queries the resolver sent to authority servers for this query.
How a query was answered: from a zone the node serves.
How a query was answered: from the cache.
How a query was answered: from the cache of proven non-existence.
How a query was answered: from an expired cache entry because the upstreams failed.
How a query was answered: by a forwarder.
How a query was answered: by the recursive resolver.
How a query was answered: from local data of the resolver.
How a query was answered: by a policy such as a block list.
How a query was answered: refused.
